The sheer magnitude of love and meticulous craftsmanship poured into this game is nothing short of breathtaking, yet it's all the more disheartening to consider how REmake3 ultimately unfolded in comparison to this one. Despite its flaws, one can't help but be captivated by the myriad elements the game executes with finesse. From its meticulously crafted scenarios to the intricately designed enemies and the immersive atmosphere that envelops you, there's an undeniable allure to the experience. While I am tempted to delve deeper into a comprehensive review, I know all too well that the game does not need publicity.

Fabulous game. The forest and village are especially well-realized with gorgeous graphics and a moody atmosphere. The combat is clean and, after I figured out how to knife parry, I felt very powerful. But still, there are some tense sections that kept me on edge.

The characters are great. Ashley is completely adorable, and Luis and Ada each have fun ways of remaining both mysterious and charming. And our hero, Leon, is a real hoot. The plot isn't anything special, but a big plus is that you really don't have to know anything about other Resident Evil games to understand this one. It's a straightforward rescue mission that turns into discovering new threats.

Don't expect to be spooked. This is an action game more than anything survival or horror. Although, despite me saying that, I think the quieter sections of the game are its best parts: rain falling on the village's hidden shrines, secret rooms tucked away in the castle, and the creeping laboratories of the island. It's really special.

I strongly recommend this game. I think you're sure to find something about it that you love, too!

overall though even with me considering a few things that i consider personally to be areas the game heavily lacks in or is flawed like its characters and story the game is still above average and if anyone does enjoy those areas of the game then they will likely have a great time

I see no more reason to recommend other people to play the original RE4. The controls are dated and it doesn't bring really anything to the table that the new remake doesn't do better. RE2 and 3 I still recommend the originals as they're vastly different experience than the remakes. But for 4 this is not the case at all.

Graphics and performance are as we are used to from RE2 and RE3 remake => no complaints and only praise.

All in all great job by Capcom.

About 3 years after it's release the game now uses a shady Russian DRM called "The Enigma Protector" and performance is now worse than it was with Denuvo. It also created compatibility issues with community beloved mods. Extremely disappointing customer practices.

This Resident Evil 4 REMAKE is a careful restoration of what remains one of the most compelling action games ever made. As an avid Resident evil 4 fan having beaten the original hundreds of times. The remake has done an absolutely outstanding job re-imaging the original story in a new light. Game feels great, combat is lively, active, exciting. I can see myself dumping in hundreds of hours playing through multiple times just as I did the original. Highly recommended but I think beating the original first before playing the remake certainly leaves your memory fresh to identify the more subtle differences and to recognize what they've brought back as easter eggs, though not necessary. Capcom really went above and beyond with this one and i'm glad they did. I can't wait to see separate ways brought back and how they'll re-imagine ada's part in the story next.
